name: SCCW Universal Championship
epitaph: The SCCW Universal Championship's first recorded champion is Evan 'Damage' Jackson. The fed's own record carries 21 reigns on it, across 12 different champions. The longest is Aimz's, 421 days from 2 August 2008. Two of its reigns ended outside a match — stripped from the holder or vacated. The belt left Lane Stevens on 13 June 2010, stripped from the holder, and the surviving record carries no later change.

name: SCCW Gateway Championship
epitaph: The SCCW Gateway Championship's first recorded champion is Jonathan Rhine. The fed's own record carries 14 reigns on it, across 14 different champions. The longest is Phillip Kennedy's, 195 days from 11 January 2009. Baron von Blackberry held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: SCCW LiveWire Championship
epitaph: The SCCW LiveWire Championship was first won by Evan 'Damage' Jackson on 12 November 2005. The fed's own record carries 34 reigns on it, across 31 different champions. The longest is Jadian Bridden's, 161 days from 27 September 2009. Two of its reigns ended outside a match — stripped from the holder or vacated. Mitchell Quinlan held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: SCCW SIN Championships
epitaph: The SCCW SIN Championships' first recorded champion is Cowboys From Hell. The fed's own record carries 9 reigns on it, across 9 different champions. The longest is Lance Marshall and Desade's, 141 days from 25 July 2009. Daddy Daughter Day held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Fuse Custom Chaos Champion
epitaph: The Fuse Custom Chaos Champion was first won by The Animal on 6 November 2005. The fed's own record carries 12 reigns on it, across 12 different champions. The longest is Evan 'Damage' Jackson's, 73 days from 6 September 2006. Two of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. Jonathan Rhine held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Fuse Fusion Championship
epitaph: The Fuse Fusion Championship's first recorded champion is Ethan Frost, who was already carrying it when the fed's own record opens on him. Its Fusion Rumble of 10 February 2007 ended with Frost and Fred Fusion eliminated together and the two of them declared co-holders. The fed's own record carries four reigns on it, across three champions: Frost alone, Frost and Fusion twice, and The Legacy. Frost and Fusion held it at the end of the surviving record, by then billed under a name its own authority figure refused to recognise.
notes: Self-awarded on the federation's own word: FUSE's own commentary opens the double-title ladder match of Afflicted Glory 2007 (31 May 2007) with "It's time for our first title match of the night! True, both belts up for grabs are unsanctioned, but both of these teams feel passionately about their belts". The same broadcast stages the FUSION straps as belts hung above the ring that the fed itself had not sanctioned for two months and puts them up against the Fatal Affliction straps the reigning team had made for itself, the losing set "banned" from FUSE; the preceding segment, "FUSION Wrestling: RIP", bills the pair as "the Fatal Affliction or FUSION Wrestling titles" and shows the Reeds wearing their own custom straps.

name: Fuse Fatal Faction
epitaph: The Fuse Fatal Faction was first won by Critical Error on 18 November 2006. The fed's own record carries 8 reigns on it, across 6 different champions. The longest is Cowboys From Hell's, 78 days from 19 July 2007. One of its reigns ended outside a match — retired with the belt. SCCW retired it on 5 October 2007.

events.note: the federation's own authority figure suspended the reigning Fatal Faction Champions and retired the championship. Recorded outside the booking system: the log row carries no card link and the fields 'Uproar 10/05' / 'Segment: The Last Stand', dated 5 Oct 2007. The belt's own last reign ends `retired` on the same day. Source: The fed's own title log, the fed's own legacy record line.
